tldr: Two-sided finite-sample calibration for binary regression discontinuity can be strictly conservative when its two tails are maximized under incompatible Lipschitz null laws. On every rational design with five distinct sites per arm and positive prescribed weights normalized within each arm, an ordered-site active-face reduction exactly computes the joint envelope \(\kappa\) and the common separate-tail value \(\psi\), giving the necessary-and-sufficient strict-gain criterion \(\kappa<\alpha\) and \(\psi>\alpha/2\). Complete real algebraic elimination is imported machinery used to evaluate this reduction. As a concrete corollary, a radius-\(1/1000\) neighborhood of a heterogeneous reference design has joint envelope below \(1/10\), each separate extreme above \(1/20\), and deficit exceeding \(4/125\); joint calibration rejects both extremes while the ISY equal-tail rule rejects no statistic value.
